config.title: Build blue green deploy readiness endpoint set

intro.title: Build blue green deploy readiness endpoint set
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a set of readiness endpoints for a blue-green deployment system using Node.js. You will create a simple Express server with two separate endpoints: one for the 'blue' environment and one for the 'green' environment, each returning a status to indicate if it is ready to serve traffic. The core programming concept involves setting up HTTP servers, defining route handlers, and managing basic application state to simulate deployment readiness. You will use key Node.js technologies like the Express framework and the built-in HTTP module to handle web requests. By the end, you will understand how to implement and test readiness checks that are essential for safe, zero-downtime deployments.
intro.usecase: Blue-green deployment readiness endpoints are critical in production systems where zero-downtime updates are required, such as e-commerce platforms during holiday sales or banking applications processing transactions 24/7. Developers implement these health-check endpoints in deployment dashboards and CI/CD pipelines to validate that new versions can safely handle live traffic before switching over. For example, a streaming service like Netflix uses readiness probes to ensure new recommendation algorithms work correctly before directing users to updated servers, preventing service disruptions during global releases.

objectives: Construct a basic Express server with two separate endpoints for blue and green deployments
Configure environment variables to control which deployment version is currently active
Implement a readiness check endpoint that returns the status of the active deployment
Initialize a version tracking system to distinguish between blue and green deployments
Apply conditional logic to route traffic based on deployment status
Manipulate response headers to indicate deployment version in API responses
Integrate a simple health monitoring mechanism for both deployment environments

steps.title: Initialize server configuration
steps.instruction: Inside the createServer function, define two constants: one named PORT with a value of 3000, and another named ENVIRONMENT_STATUS with a value of 'ready'.
steps.hint: Use the const keyword to declare constants. Place them at the top of your function body.
steps.expectedOutcome: Your createServer function will have two constants defined: PORT set to 3000 and ENVIRONMENT_STATUS set to 'ready'.
successCriteria: The createServer function contains constants named PORT (value 3000) and ENVIRONMENT_STATUS (value 'ready').
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully initialized the server configuration with the required constants.

steps.feedbackWrong: The configuration constants are missing or incorrect. Please define PORT as 3000 and ENVIRONMENT_STATUS as 'ready' inside the createServer function.

steps.title: Create readiness check handler
steps.instruction: Inside the createServer function, create a function named handleReadinessCheck that takes request and response parameters and returns a 200 OK response with a JSON body containing { status: 'ready' }.
steps.hint: Define a function that sets the response status code to 200, sets the Content-Type header to 'application/json', and sends a JSON response.
steps.expectedOutcome: A handleReadinessCheck function is defined inside createServer that properly returns a 200 OK JSON response.
successCriteria: The handleReadinessCheck function exists, takes req and res parameters, sets status 200, sets Content-Type header, and sends JSON with { status: 'ready' }.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the readiness check handler that will respond to /ready endpoint requests.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've started the handler function. Make sure it sets the correct status code, headers, and returns the proper JSON response.
steps.feedbackWrong: The readiness handler isn't properly implemented. Check that the function takes request/response parameters and returns a 200 OK JSON response.

steps.expectedOutcome: The handleHealth function is defined inside createServer, ready to be used as a route handler for the /health endpoint.
successCriteria: A function named handleHealth exists inside createServer, sets the Content-Type header to 'application/json', and returns a JSON object with status 'healthy' and environment status.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the health check handler that will return environment status.

steps.feedbackWrong: The health check handler isn't properly defined. Check that you've created a function named handleHealth inside createServer with the correct implementation.

steps.title: Set up request routing
steps.instruction: Inside the createServer function, implement the main request handler function that checks URL paths and routes requests to the appropriate endpoint handler.

steps.title: Create and configure HTTP server
steps.instruction: Inside the createServer function, create an HTTP server instance using http.createServer() and pass your main request handler to it.
steps.hint: Use the http module's createServer method, which takes your request handler function as an argument.
steps.expectedOutcome: The createServer function now contains an HTTP server instance configured with your request handler.
successCriteria: An HTTP server instance is created using http.createServer(requestHandler) inside the createServer function.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the HTTP server instance with your request handler.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track. Make sure you're using http.createServer() and passing the requestHandler function as an argument.
steps.feedbackWrong: The HTTP server instance wasn't created correctly. Remember to use http.createServer(requestHandler) inside the createServer function.

steps.title: Start the server
steps.instruction: Inside the createServer function, after creating the HTTP server instance, call server.listen() with the PORT constant and add a console.log message that indicates the server is running.
steps.hint: Use server.listen(PORT, () => { console.log(...) }) to start the server and log a startup message.
steps.expectedOutcome: The server will be configured to listen on the specified port and log a startup message when it begins accepting connections.
successCriteria: server.listen() is called with PORT and includes a callback that logs a startup message to the console.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully started the server with a startup log message. The server is now ready to accept requests on the configured port.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you're calling server.listen() with the PORT constant and including a callback function that logs a message to the console.
steps.feedbackWrong: The server isn't properly started. Check that you're calling server.listen() with the PORT constant and adding a console.log message in the callback.

steps.title: Export and run the server
steps.instruction: Inside the createServer function, add the server.start() call to start listening on the configured port, then export the function and add a conditional to run it when the file is executed directly.
steps.hint: Call server.listen(PORT) to start the server. Use module.exports to export createServer. Check if the current module is the main one with require.main === module.
steps.expectedOutcome: The server function is exported and can be started when the file is run directly, completing the blue-green deploy readiness endpoint set.
successCriteria: The createServer function includes server.listen(PORT), is exported with module.exports, and has a conditional that runs it when require.main === module.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully exported the server function and made it runnable directly, completing your readiness endpoint set.
